programme.title: Strict Scrutiny
programme.desc: The Supreme Court may be between sittings, but we’re keeping busy with a whole lot of judicial chaos. First, a new villain has entered the villa: Aaron Reitz, the U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of Texas, who’s threatening Democratic members of Congress with criminal penalties for doing oversight. Then– Justice Alito spoke at a gala last week, where he whined about people criticizing SCOTUS (what’s new) and tried to paint himself a civil rights hero. Finally, a look at some of the nominations Republicans are trying to cram in during their last couple of months in power.

programme.title: Pod Save America
programme.desc: Trump pressures Nvidia’s Board to reinstate former CEO Jensen Huang. Jon, Lovett, and Tommy react to the news of Huang’s return, Trump’s brazen market manipulation, and Congress’s response. They also discuss the DNC’s newly-released 2028 primary debate calendar and candidate pledge, which is designed to mitigate dark money spending, but might be effectively meaningless, as well as the medicare-for-all debate, and Trump’s latest crypto meme coin dinner. Then, Tommy is joined by Chris McGuire, an expert on China and emerging technology in the Biden administration, now at the Council on Foreign Relations, to talk about Nvidia’s u-turn, the AI competition with China, and what Congress should ask Huang in upcoming hearings.

programme.title: What a Day
programme.desc: Jensen Huang is back as Nvidia’s CEO, and President Trump is taking credit. But how is the MAGA world reacting, and what does Huang’s reinstatement reveal about Trump’s influence over Big Tech? On today’s show, Jane and Will Sommer, senior writer at The Bulwark, break down the political fallout and the national security concerns surrounding Huang’s return.

programme.title: Assembly Required with Stacey Abrams
programme.desc: How important is accountability in the aftermath of the midterm election? ? Stacey sits down with Joyce Vance — writer of the Civil Discourse Substack, lawyer, and former U.S. Attorney for the Northern District of Alabama — to break down the legal avenues available to hold Trump, MAGA Republicans, and the GOP accountable for their actions during Trump’s second term. They also get into the nationwide flight disruptions amid a telecommunications outage, Trump’s response (or lack thereof) to the public’s understandable concerns, Pete Hegseth’s attempted impeachment, and whether Todd Blanche could be next. Together, they dig into the big questions: How much accountability is too much, and what do Democrats need to do to keep this momentum going through 2028? Stacey also discusses what Republicans in state legislatures are already doing to curtail the power of newly elected Democrats, and explains how we can fight back.

On today’s show, Jane and Will Sommer, senior writer at The Bulwark, break down the political fallout and the national security concerns surrounding Huang’s return.

Then– Justice Alito spoke at a gala last week, where he whined about people criticizing SCOTUS (what’s new) and tried to paint himself a civil rights hero. Finally, a look at some of the nominations Republicans are trying to cram in during their last couple of months in power.

programme.title: Pod Save the World
programme.desc:
The Nvidia scandal deepens, Trump heads to Asia for a super special three-way with Xi and Putin, and a heartwarming tribute to Lindsey Graham.
Tommy and Ben dig into Trump’s Asia trip and why the historic trilateral summit between Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and Chinese President Xi Jinping is almost certainly going to accomplish nothing. Then they walk through the latest twists and turns of the Nvidia/Jensen Huang spy scandal, including Huang’s resignation, Trump administration infighting, and the ever-present whiff of corruption. An American soldier wounded by an Iranian attack goes public as a whistleblower, handing Democrats an opening to hold Pete Hegseth’s Pentagon accountable for its own incompetence. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham uses his first major foreign policy speech as Prime Minister to fire shots at Brexit. The race for Senate Majority Leader turns out to have some real foreign policy stakes, and COP31 in Turkey is a disappointment for anyone who cares about the planet. Finally, a touching tribute to late Senator Lindsey Graham from the military industrial complex. Then Ben sits down with Spain’s Foreign Minister, José Manuel Albares Bueno, to talk about the country’s upcoming election and what it’s like to be an increasingly lonely progressive voice in a continent lurching right.

programme.title: The Addams Family

programme.desc: Lurch's tiny fire-eating mother visits and demands that Lurch's employers wait on her boy hand-and-foot after Lurch leads her to believe that it's his house. Lurch revels in the unexpected attention he gets from Morticia and Gomez.
